scenarios.title: The deal moves on during dinner.
scenarios.lede: Five business exports and a catalogue, four entities, three views, one Process. The CRM marks the deal ready; the decision reaches the PWA, « Traiter » (handle) goes out as a webhook and the customer email follows.

scenarios.title: One customer, two systems, no shared identifier.
scenarios.lede: An ERP, a CRM, one Entity. Email matches the records; a shared mailbox opens an ambiguity. lumnik does not pick: a person decides, and the decision holds on replay.

scenarios.title: An established customer does not change records in silence.
scenarios.lede: Yesterday, CRM contact CC-42 and ERP account AC-700 both meant Nova Pumps. Today its email points to Helios Valves. lumnik does not move the contact: it makes it ambiguous, and a person decides.

scenarios.title: A critical unassigned incident reaches the manager's inbox.
scenarios.lede: One CMMS CSV export, a Connector, a Workflow, a Process. One decision, only one; the assignment moves it forward.

scenarios.title: The catalogue reaches the partner in their format, not ours.
scenarios.lede: Two ERP CSV files, products and categories, are joined in the hub and delivered to S3 in a partner's format: French headers, semicolons, decimal commas, recoded statuses, a masked internal reference. A receipt proves the delivered bytes.

scenarios.title: One product record, two databases: PostgreSQL and Oracle stay where they are.
scenarios.lede: Products live in PostgreSQL, their categories in Oracle. Two jdbc connectors read them without writing to either, and one entity joins them: 40,234 products, each with its category when there is one.

scenarios.title: Question 40,000 products, with the SQL shown.
scenarios.lede: Two CSV exports, one entity, an app reduced to chat. The question becomes a read-only query; the answer shows its SQL.

scenarios.title: 40,000 products, browsed page by page.
scenarios.lede: Two CSV exports, two entities, two linked views, one app. The hub serves the catalogue 50 rows at a time; the PWA never loads more.

scenarios.title: Search 40,000 products, facets included.
scenarios.lede: Two CSV exports, one entity, a SearchIndex, an app reduced to search. The hub indexes the declared columns; the PWA filters by facet.
